entities.name: MP Materials

thesis.summary: Only US mine-to-magnet integrated REE producer; government price floor + Apple offtake.
thesis.detail: The cornerstone US rare-earth holding. The only fully integrated mine-to-magnet producer in the Western Hemisphere (Mountain Pass, CA + Fort Worth magnets). The Pentagon is the largest shareholder (~15%, $400M) with a 10-yr NdPr price floor (~$110/kg), a $150M loan, and a $500M Apple magnet offtake ($200M prepaid). Record NdPr output and revenue doubling YoY. Trades at a very high multiple and is still loss-making, so the strategic floor — not the current P&L — is the thesis. Catalysts: magnet ramp into the Jan-2027 DFARS defense deadline, 10X expansion. Risk: extreme valuation, NdPr price swings.

catalysts.description: Magnet ramp into DFARS defense-sourcing deadline — Q2-2026 (Aug 6): Independence delivered magnets to GM for qualification testing; initial commercial shipments still expected Q4 2026, then gradual ramp; magnet start-up costs $14.4M in Q2

entities.name: Energy Fuels
entities.govt_support: DPA Title III eligible; AUD80M (Donald); DoW Office of Strategic Capital $725M conditional loan commitment (signed Jun 18 2026) for RE metals/alloy facility + White Mesa metallization buildout

thesis.summary: Largest US uranium producer AND only US heavy-REE separation; fortress balance sheet.
thesis.detail: A rare dual critical-minerals play: America's largest uranium producer AND the only US facility separating heavy rare earths (first commercial Dy and Tb oxides in 2026). Fortress balance sheet (~$910M, ~no debt). White Mesa Mill (UT) is the hub; targeting some of the lowest-cost NdPr in the world (~$29/kg vs. the ~$110 floor). World-class Toliara feedstock (Madagascar). Catalysts: REE commercial circuit (~2027), Phase-2 expansion, uranium price. Risk: REE not yet commercial; Madagascar jurisdiction; multi-project execution.

catalysts.description: Commercial heavy-REE (Dy/Tb) separation - Aug 19 2026: terbium oxide produced at the White Mesa Mill (UT) passed ALL qualification testing by the largest permanent-magnet manufacturer in Japan, which confirmed it meets specification and is approved for use in commercial rare-earth permanent-magnet production with no further qualification or validation required. First customer qualification of a US-produced 'heavy' rare earth; Tb oxide ~$5.5M/tonne (Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, CIF Europe). No offtake volume, price or contract disclosed - this is a specification gate, not revenue.
White Mesa Phase 2 heavy-REE expansion FID — construction began Jul 29, 2026 (~$104M mill expansion; Phase 1 circuits up to 20 tpa Tb / 120 tpa Dy targeted end-2027, Sm/Eu/Gd end-2028)
DoW OSC $725M conditional loan → domestic RE metals/alloy (metallization) facility

Company guidance has been CLOSE IN EARLY 2027 since the Jun 23 2026 definitive agreement - 'The transaction is expected to close in early 2027 subject to customary closing conditions, including the receipt of applicable regulatory approvals, including foreign investment, antitrust and other government approvals' - and the Aug 5 2026 Q2 release restates the same early-2027 expectation. Close US$299M all-scrip acquisition of Australian Strategic Materials (announced Jan 20, 2026) — COMPLETED Aug 28, 2026. ASM securityholders approved at the Aug 12 Perth scheme meetings; Federal Court of Australia approved both the Share Scheme and Option Scheme; schemes effective Aug 19-20; ASX suspension at the close of Aug 19 and removal from official quotation Aug 31. thesis.summary: Largest, lowest-cost lithium producer; max operating leverage to a price recovery.
thesis.detail: The blue-chip lithium recovery play. World's largest, lowest-cost producer — maximum operating leverage to a price rebound, as Q1 2026 showed (EPS swung from a 2025 loss to a strong beat as carbonate roughly doubled). ~$2.7B liquidity, paid down $1.3B debt, pays a dividend; a $90M DoD award supports the Kings Mountain (NC) restart. Catalysts: sustained lithium-price recovery, Kings Mountain permitting, cost cuts. Risk: highly cyclical/price-sensitive; large-cap, so less multibagger torque than the juniors.

thesis.summary: The pure-play US enrichment monopoly federally funded to replace Russian supply.
thesis.detail: The strategic choke-point play. The only US-owned, US-technology enrichment company (Piketon, OH), making both LEU and HALEU — the fuel advanced reactors need and that Russia has dominated. A ~$900M DOE task order (plus up to ~$170M more) funds commercial HALEU; first significant US HALEU already delivered. The Russian-enrichment ban is a structural tailwind. Catalysts: more DOE/utility contracts, expansion financing, advanced-reactor offtakes. Risk: extreme volatility; appropriations-dependent; capacity not online until ~2029.

catalysts.description: Commercial HALEU capacity online at Piketon

entities.name: Almonty Industries

thesis.summary: Only Western-aligned listed tungsten producer ramping into a 2027 US defense import ban.
thesis.detail: The only Western-aligned, US-listed producing tungsten company. Sangdong (South Korea) — one of the largest, highest-grade deposits — began mining late 2025 and formally commissioned March 2026; revenue +221% YoY in Q1 with positive EBITDA. Acquired a Montana project and is relocating HQ to the US, with a binding offtake to supply tungsten oxide solely for US defense ahead of a 2027 ban on Chinese tungsten in defense. ~$260M cash. Catalysts: Sangdong ramp (revenue projected to surge), Montana, EXIM financing. Risk: ramp execution; convertible-debenture volatility.

catalysts.description: Sangdong ramp to nameplate (revenue surge) — mill commenced processing operations Jul 1, 2026, treating ~139.7kt stockpile @ ~0.25% WO3; company transitions to saleable tungsten concentrate producer. Jun 2026: $800M convertible senior notes (2.25% due 2031) raised; joined Russell 1000/3000 Jun 29. Q2'26 (Aug 2026 6-K): revenue $43.0M (+498% y/y) at tungsten ~$3,075/MTU — ramp monetizing. NOTE: new shelf registration filed Aug 2026 (potential future equity issuance); ASX delisting final trade Aug 28, 2026. Shelf sized ~US$246.79M (filed Aug 11, 2026), including an ESOP/employee-equity component — earmarked for Sangdong Phase I optimization, potential Phase II and the adjacent molybdenum project. CAPITAL ALLOCATION PIVOT: on Aug 17, 2026 the board approved a new share repurchase program of up to US$300M / 14.4M shares (~5% of shares outstanding as of Aug 14), running 36 months from Aug 24, 2026 via Nasdaq open market and ATSs — announced ~1 week after the ~US$246.79M shelf, so buyback authorization now exceeds shelf capacity; shares +6-7% on the day.

US defense tungsten import ban takes effect (Jan 1, 2027: DoD procurement barred from China/Russia/Iran/North Korea tungsten). PRECURSOR POLICY NOW IN FORCE — BIS temporary final rule (published Federal Register Aug 6, 2026) is EFFECTIVE Aug 27, 2026 through Aug 27, 2027: US persons selling tungsten waste and scrap (and black mass) must allocate 100% of monthly sales to US persons absent a BIS adjustment/exception. Implements the Jul 30, 2026 Presidential Determination under DPA Sec. 101; company-specific exceptions available on a rolling basis (BIS targets 14-day responses); public comments due Nov 4, 2026. Effect: removes recycled/scrap tungsten units from the export market and tightens ex-China Western primary-tungsten demand ahead of the 2027 ban — supportive of Sangdong's contracted APT pricing. Second-order/indirect for ALM (it is a primary concentrate producer, not a US scrap seller); no company guidance change.
GTP offtake expanded to US$490M contracted annual revenue at current APT pricing; term 15->21 yrs; volume +40% to 4.41M MTU (Jul 14, 2026)

invalidation_triggers: Tungsten price normalizes if China curbs ease
